title: Heat Pump
description: Clock-synced sidechain ducking: hold + log release
text:
Heat Pump is a clock-synced sidechain ducking envelope: on each division the CV ducks, holds briefly, then recovers with a logarithmic release. Patch CV Out to a filter or VCA; MIDI CC mirrors when Out is enabled.

Main sets release speed. Shift + fader sets depth. Button + fader picks clock division. Short tap triggers one manual duck. Long press mutes without snapping to idle. Shift + long toggles invert.

channels.jackDescription: CV Out = duck envelope; CV In modulates Depth, Release, or triggers Duck.

title: Grooves
description: Multi-genre MIDI drum grooves with feel
text: Grooves is a one-channel multi-genre drum helper with up to seven MIDI voices clock-synced in 4/4. **Groove** picks the genre family; **Density** and **Feel** shape fills and character; **Drummer** personas (long press) change ornament style. Swing depth is capped by **Swing max %** (sign = direction). Jack modes include Any/Stacked CV out and CV in for Density, Feel, or Reset. Clock-driven scheduling stays in a dedicated processor; MIDI sends run in a separate task (`pending_*` isolation).

channels.jackDescription: Any: velocity-weighted pulse per hit. Stacked: 1 V kick, 2 V snare, 4 V hats.
channels.faderDescription: Reveals extra drum hits as ghosts.
channels.fnPlusShiftDescription: Short: reverse swing. Long: Any vs Stacked.

title: Echolot
description: MIDI/CV delay with feedback and pitch shift
text:
Echolot is a MIDI/CV delay with feedback, mix, and optional pitch shift on each repeat.

### Cheatsheet

Delay with feedback and optional pitch intervals. I/O picks MIDI/CV routing; Ping-Pong alternates MIDI Out A/B (MIDI→MIDI and CV→MIDI). Mute = ring-out (block new input; queue plays out). Long Panic clears the trail — Third interval edits never panic that hold. MIDI In always flashes white for diagnosis when muted.

**Faders**

- **Main** — Delay (up = shorter / faster)

**Buttons**

- **Long** — Panic (clear queue); skipped if Third used this hold

**LEDs**

- White flash on MIDI/gate in (~20% when muted)
- Ping-Pong: Top = Out A · Bottom = Out B

**Params**

- Routing: Single / Ping-Pong

channels.jackDescription: Role depends on I/O and Signal params.

title: Control Issues
description: Shape CV and send it as MIDI control
text:
Control Issues shapes CV (linear, log, exp, S-curve, rectify, fold) and sends MIDI CC or NRPN. Supports slew, quantization, and gate or continuous input modes.

### Cheatsheet

1-channel CV→MIDI sculptor. Defaults are transparent (+100 % att, 0 offset, 0 slew, Linear, full CC window, 100 Hz). Gate mode runs a Schmitt threshold (0.1 V hysteresis) then the same pipeline. Mute sends Output Min once and goes silent; unmute resends the live value. Watch the button LED for level — fader LEDs stay dark. Uses clock ticker only (no CLOCK_PUBSUB). No clock → no downbeat blink.

**Faders**

- **Main** — Attenuverter −100…+100 % (center deadband = 0)

**Buttons**

- **Shift+Hold** — momentary Bypass (keeps Range / Min-Max / Rate)

**Params / LEDs**

- Button LED only: Main = app color × out; Alt = red × |offset|; Third = cyan × slew (floor so hue stays visible at 0)

channels.jackDescription: Bipolar or unipolar CV in; shaped value as MIDI CC/NRPN.
channels.faderDescription: Main fader controls shaping parameters per latch layer.

title: Venn
description: Dual Euclidean layers + boolean logic; scale-aware melody via Extent
text:
Two independent Euclidean masks combined with boolean logic — the OXI GEN
dual-layer idea with a scale-aware melodic line. Color sets Layer A; Layer B
LEDs use a fixed complement. Btn1 shows logic mode, not Color. Different
lengths per layer enable polyrhythmic XOR/AND patterns Euclid cannot make alone.

Melody: Note A is degree 0 of the device quantizer key. Extent is the arch span
in scale degrees through Length-A; Interval B is diatonic steps above that line
for Ch2 (wire indices 0–12 unchanged). Extent 0 = monotone Note A.

Needs clock. Prob % < 100 adds optional flakiness; 100 is fully deterministic.
No pitch CV (use GenSeq for that).

Venn always draws its degrees from the device Scale. **Follow device tonic** (default on) adds the missing half: hold the Scene button and move Fader 5 and both lines transpose, together with Bassment, Contura, Chord Vamp and Arp de Lévy. The pitch class comes from the device, the octave stays with MIDI Note A, and the change lands at the start of the next A-cycle rather than mid-pattern.

### Cheatsheet

**Faders**

- **Main** — F0 pulses A · F1 pulses B (density; absolute pulse count, Bjorklund redistributes)

**Buttons**

- **Shift+Btn2** — Toggle post-logic invert (shadow); white↔none fade like Heat Pump

channels.faderDescription: Number of pulses in Euclidean layer A (density)
channels.faderPlusFnDescription: Cycle length for layer A and melody phase (2–32)
channels.faderPlusShiftDescription: Scale-degree span above Note A (0–24 degrees, device key)

channels.faderPlusShiftDescription: Diatonic steps above the melodic line for Ch2 (0–12)

channels.ledBottom: Coupled with logic meters / length hue

title: Manifold
description: One CV in, three shaped outs with comparator modes
text:
One CV in, three shaped outs. Each out is independently CV, Gate or Trigger: CV gets attenuverter / offset / slew, Gate and Trigger get threshold / hysteresis / pulse length. A long press on channels 1–3 cycles that out through CV → Gate → Trigger right on the device, and the change is stored as a parameter, so the configurator stays in sync. Shift + long press on an out cycles its output range; the button flashes once for ±5 V or twice for 0–10 V to confirm the new setting. Channel 0 freezes the conditioned input on a short tap; channels B/C/D mute on a short tap.

With nothing patched into the input, channel 0 turns into a morphing LFO and drives B/C/D on its own once the jack has been still for about 1.2 s — movement on the jack switches back to CV in. Same wave engine as Super LFO, with speed, morph and skew on the three channel 0 fader layers (Main = speed, Alt = morph, Third = skew) and Shift + short press for clock sync. *LFO Speed* moves the whole rate range down to Slow or Slowest.

All four waves — the conditioned input on channel 0 plus the three outs B, C and D — mirror to MIDI. Channel 0 and any out in CV mode always send CC. On Gate or Trigger outs, *Mode Map* can switch a lane to Note instead: one bit per out (B in bit 0, C in bit 1, D in bit 2); when set, that lane sends Note On/Off on edges and the pitch comes from that lane’s *CC Map* slot (7-bit note number). *Mode Map* 0 keeps every lane on CC (legacy). By default they share the base *MIDI Channel* and take *MIDI CC* + 0…3. *Ch Map* and *CC Map* break that up: *Ch Map* packs one nibble per wave (wave 0 in bits 0–3, wave 1 in bits 4–7, …), value + 1 = MIDI channel 1…16; *CC Map* packs 7 bits per wave (wave 0 in bits 0–6, wave 1 in bits 7–13, …) holding the CC number directly (or the note number when *Mode Map* selects Note for that lane). A map of 0 means “all waves follow the base”, which is the shipped default and bit-for-bit the old behaviour. Example: channels 1, 5, 9 and 13 → nibbles 0, 4, 8, 12 → 0 + 4·16 + 8·256 + 12·4096 = 51 264; CCs 20, 21, 40, 41 → 20 + 21·128 + 40·16384 + 41·2097152 = 86 641 300. A CC Map field is seven bits wide, so it reaches CC 0–127 only; in NRPN mode the base CC still spans the full 14-bit range, a mapped one does not.

LEDs use five equidistant hues running from blue through violet and red to orange, one per operating mode. Channel 0 is blue while CV in feeds the outs and one step warmer once the internal LFO takes over; the outs take the remaining three steps by mode — CV, then Gate, then Trigger in orange — so a mode swap is visible the moment it lands. All four channels dim with signal amplitude.

title: Ripppple
description: Root CV or LFO through three cumulative waveshapers
text:
Ripppple is a cumulative waveshaper chain, not four independent LFOs. Channel 0 is the root: its jack is a CV input with attenuverter conditioning — Main trims, Alt offsets, Third slews. When the jack has been static for about 1.2 s the input falls back to an internal morphing LFO; jack movement switches back to CV in immediately, and the same three fader layers become speed, morph and skew instead. A short tap on channel 0 freezes the root value — the value itself, so stepped morph nodes hold too — and Shift plus a short tap toggles clock sync while the internal LFO runs.

Channels 1–3 have no oscillators of their own. Each stage waveshapes the cumulative result of everything before it: B shapes the root, C shapes B’s output, D shapes C’s output. The jacks and MIDI CCs mirror that chain — what you hear on output D has passed through every preceding stage. Stage faders are always Main = amount, Alt = offset, Third = slew. At amount zero, Fold passes through at unity gain; Soft and Rect blend from dry input towards their curve. A long press cycles that stage’s process through Fold → Soft → Rect — the same three choices as the params “Process B”, “Process C” and “Process D” in the configurator, which set the start value and follow a live long press. Shift plus a long press cycles the output range ±5 V ↔ 0–10 V; the button flashes once for ±5 V or twice for 0–10 V. A short tap mutes with a click-free ramp. Moving the fader while the button is held scrubs the Third layer and cancels a pending mute or process cycle on release.

The LEDs meter the chain. Top and bottom form a bipolar display of each stage’s cumulative output. Five equidistant hues separate the operating modes: channel 0 is one hue for CV in and another while the internal LFO drives it; channels 1–3 take the hue of their active process — Fold, Soft or Rect — so a process swap is visible at a glance. Button LEDs on channels 1–3 breathe with the stage output even while Shift is held. Muted channels dim heavily and their button LED goes dark; channel 0’s button stays bright while the chain is frozen. All four channels can mirror their level as MIDI CC or NRPN, using the base CC plus the channel offset.

Two packed params break the single-channel assumption when you need it. “Ch Map” holds one nibble per wave — wave 0 in bits 0–3, wave 1 in bits 4–7, and so on — where the stored nibble plus one is the MIDI channel 1–16. “CC Map” holds one 7-bit field per wave in the same order, wave w at bits 7·w to 7·w+6, giving each wave its own CC number 0–127. A map of 0 as a whole means “follow the base”: Ch Map 0 sends every wave on the MIDI Channel param, CC Map 0 keeps the old base-CC-plus-offset derivation, and both default to 0, so an untouched Ripppple behaves exactly as before. For a worked example, to put the root on channel 1, stage B on channel 10 and the other two on channel 16, write the nibbles 0, 9, 15, 15, which is 0 + 9·16 + 15·256 + 15·4096 = 65 424. To send CCs 20, 21, 40 and 41, write 20 + 21·128 + 40·16384 + 41·2 097 152 = 86 641 300. Note that a CC Map field is seven bits wide, so it can only reach CC 0–127 — in NRPN mode the base CC still spans the full 14-bit range, but a mapped one does not.

title: Dit Dah
description: ITU Morse phrase player with 16th-quantized note-ons
text:
Dit Dah plays packed ASCII Morse phrases as MIDI notes, quantized so each dit/dah starts on a 16th. It needs clock: MIDI Start/Reset or the first 16th after ticks appear (analog clock on Atom/Meteor/Cube has no transport) arms playback; after that the phrase loops without waiting for bar resets. Stop silences everything.

Jack is one CV: CV Out Gate, CV Out Pitch (0–10 V, V/Oct), CV In Gate (±5 V rising edge arms like long press), or CV In Dit length / Pitch offset / Dah interval. CV In dests add ±5 V bipolar on top of the saved fader at playback — not written to storage. Unpatched ±5 V ≈ centre, so no change. MIDI notes always fire.

Main sets dit length from a 30 ms floor up to four 16ths of the current tick. Dahs last three dits. Alt transposes the whole phrase. Third (deadzone) adds the Dah interval param only onto dahs. ITU gaps (1 / 3 / 7) stay; invert only swaps tone lengths and flips the fader mappings at playback.

Short press mutes (Button LED off). Shift+short toggles texture: random MIDI velocity and swing on odd 16ths (Bottom LED white). Long press retriggers — arms the next 16th like CV In Gate. Shift+long inverts dit↔dah and flips speed/pitch at playback (Button LED white when unmuted; orange when normal). Phrase 1 defaults to SOS.

channels.jackDescription: CV Out Gate / CV Out Pitch (0–10 V V/Oct), CV In Gate (±5 V rising edge arms like long press), or CV In Dit length / Pitch offset / Dah interval (±5 V bipolar add at playback only). MIDI notes always fire.
channels.faderDescription: Duration of a dit in milliseconds, from 30 ms up to four 16th-notes of the incoming clock. Dah is 3× dit.
channels.faderPlusFnDescription: Adds the Interval param onto dahs only (deadzone around centre). Dits stay on the Alt-offset pitch.

title: Maniac Bounce
description: Delay with bounce pitch and velocity LFO
text:
Maniac Bounce is a one-channel MIDI/CV delay with dry-through, bounce pitch, and a velocity LFO on dry notes and repeats. Main sets delay time (fader up = shorter) and echo retention together — short delays fade quickly, long delays keep bouncing. Shift + fader sets the bounce interval bipolar ±24 semitones (default about +6 st). Button + fader sets Vel LFO rate and depth coupled (up = faster and deeper); the LFO modulates velocity on every note including the immediate dry hit. In MIDI→CV Gate mode the same LFO shapes gate pulse width instead.

Each note auto-gates to about half the frozen delay period. Bounce alternates +interval / −interval per repeat. A new NoteOn on the same pitch kills the prior chain for that pitch (poly with same-pitch kill). NoteOff does not kill the trail. Short button tap mutes new input while the trail rings out; long press panics unless you are holding Button+fader for Vel LFO. White button flash on input. Free-running ms delay only — no clock sync.

### Cheatsheet

**Buttons**

- **Long** — Panic (clear queue + NoteOffs); skipped if Third was used this hold

channels.jackDescription: MIDI or CV in, MIDI or CV out per I/O mode. Dry through plus bouncing repeats.
channels.faderDescription: Repeat spacing. Fader up is shorter and decays faster; down is slower with more hops.
channels.faderPlusFnDescription: Rate and depth together on dry hits and repeats. MIDI→CV Gate uses the same LFO for pulse width.
channels.fnDescription: Short mute (ring-out). Long panic unless you were editing Third.

title: Chord Vamp
description: Chord progressions — perform, shift+tap capture, or auto vamp
text:
Chord Vamp plays MIDI chord progressions in two modes. **Perform**: scrub a **pitch map** of the genre’s unique degrees across ~3 octaves and **hold** the button to sound the chord. **Auto**: a genre **rhythm phrase** (weighted hits + multi-bar rests) loops on the clock while harmony **Repeats** or **Meanders**; **short press** play/pauses. Toggle modes with **Shift + short press**.

In Perform, **Shift + short press** switches to Auto and starts playback. If the always-record ring has chords, it also commits the last N bars (per **Capture length**) into a timed clip. If the ring is empty, Auto runs the **genre phrase** instead. **Perform long press** is unused — the chord stays held while the button is down.

In Auto, **long press** clears the capture clip and reseeds the genre phrase. **Shift + long press** panics. **Shift + short press** returns to Perform.

**Feel** (Button + Fader) scales Auto hit lengths and Capture playback durations. **Swing** (scene storage, genre-seeded) delays odd 16ths; resets when you pick/reseed a genre.

**Jack** folds CV Out, CV In Macro, and CV In Panic into one enum — Macro modulates scrub (Perform) or tension (Auto); Panic fires All Notes Off from CV.

### Cheatsheet

**Faders**

- Shared axis: Dub → Disco → House → Techno → Trip-Hop → Hip-Hop → Jungle → UK Garage → Dubstep

**Jack params**

- One enum — a CV In destination and CV Out were never live at once, and the freed slot is what lets Vamp grow

**Params**

- Follow device tonic (default on)
